label: Rational authorship and epistemic ends in contingent creation
summary: Proposed unreviewed philosophical checkpoint at main 8083301a037428574d0e46b1064d8f6d858da377. Reuses #742 base-fixed net selection, #545/#555 necessitation and reason-closure boundaries, #1875 necessary bearer/contingent output and omission controls, #1380 knowledge discrimination, #737 and #1410 veracity boundaries. Distinguishes productive actual explanation, partial contrastive reasons and exhaustive determining reasons at the same whole-order explanandum. Practical authorship candidate: apprehended end, adoption for an actual reason, and intention-directed production distinguish purposive realization from post-hoc labeling and controlled lottery policy without necessarily explaining the exact endorsement contrast. Counterexample to treating the personal label as sufficient: an uncontrolled random selector within a reason-constrained policy. The same productive standard credits an impersonal producer; its modal/causal stability is compatible with reliable evidence. Normative candidate: deliberate systematic frustration of a conferred truth-directed epistemic capacity, without overriding justification, is contrary to faithfully realizing that specific end. Requires domain, normal use, genuine cognition and goodness; assertion truthfulness is not a trace-reliability theorem. No modal collapse or skepticism inferred from mere source contingency, and no actual divine application established. C2 concerns absence of n, not absence of distinct created effects. Note: docs/notes/optimal-creation-choice.md#rational-authorship-versus-brute-selection-2026-11-23-proposed-unreviewed. No new theorem, statement, definition, sourced claim, or support edge. Existing full-synthesis underdetermination retained; author-side semantic sweep only.
